## Closing as OBSOLETE per operator decision (option A)

Sequencing condition met: Gerrit 1665 (`envious-metal-budgie`) is MERGED as cd95a58d7d, and it
removed the doctor's worktree `git merge` — the very duplication this ticket existed to extract.
The doctor now folds via `merge-tree`/`commit-tree` into the published ref and never touches the
worktree, so there is no shared merge left to factor out.

The full premise disproof, with file:line citations, is in this ticket's earlier comment
"Premise validation: a BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING `reconcile_one` is not available". Summary of why
the original AC ("no duplicated merge/unrelated-history logic") is unsatisfiable as written: the
two healers hold OPPOSED policies on unrelated histories (sync refuses on a non-empty store to
prevent grafting an orphan store; the doctor unions unconditionally, pinned by a held-out test),
sync cannot adopt a ref-only merge because its consumers read ticket events off the tracker's
WORKTREE files, and their failure policies are inverted (sync must never raise; the doctor must
raise so the push path abandons). Plus an epoch-guard asymmetry and different lock scope and head
cardinality.

Rejected alternatives, recorded so this is not re-opened from scratch:

- **Thin share** (extract a ~4-line `merge_class` classifier): rejected — it buys nothing and
  couples two opposed policy domains for four lines of graph arithmetic.
- **Deep unification**: genuinely possible but NOT behaviour-preserving; it is a rewrite of the
  store's hottest path and would have to resolve the contradictory unrelated-history policy
  first. Deliberately NOT filed as follow-up work; raise it only if the duplication ever becomes
  costly.

No code change was made under this ticket.
